established_findings.finding: All six shards regressed in the same deployment window with p95 near 390-430 ms while CPU and queue occupancy remained moderate.

Reverting the new request-policy only on shard 1 lowered shard 1 p95 to 205 ms while the other five remained degraded; this is strong local causal evidence but does not by itself exclude a shared dependency.
Baseline telemetry does not directly show shared database saturation, network fabric loss, or host CPU saturation.
Control-published E_revert_s2 lowered shard 2 p95 latency to 211 ms while no other shards changed, independently replicating the shard-local recovery pattern seen in O2.

open_hypotheses.reason: O2 plus the control-published E_revert_s2 result show independent shard-local recovery after policy rollback on shards 1 and 2. Remaining shard-local experiments and at least one shared-infrastructure control are still required.

Independent local recovery on shard 2 without other shards changing is less consistent with a shared database bottleneck as the primary mechanism, but a shared additive contribution is not yet excluded without a shared-control experiment.

Independent local recovery on shard 2 without other shards changing is less consistent with a shared network regression as the primary mechanism, but a shared additive contribution is not yet excluded without a shared-control experiment.
